# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I am blind. I can feel the bomb but cannot see colors or read the manual.
The display and lights are visual elements, so I cannot perceive their state directly (they appear as [?] to me).
However, I can feel the wires. The action board lists WIRES 1, 2, and 3 with [?]. This implies I need to inspect them to know what they are, or perhaps the "DISPLAY" and "LIGHT" fields are just placeholders for information that *is* visible to others but not me.

Wait, the prompt says: "What you are shown is what your hands found... Nothing in your view is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers."
If the view shows `[?]` for wires, does that mean I don't know what they are yet? Or does it mean I need to perform an action to reveal them?
Usually, in these puzzles, the initial state description is what is currently known. If it's `[?]`, I might not have enough info to act safely.

Let's look at the other monkeys.
Mute reads the manual. Deaf sees the bomb.
I need to communicate with them.
Since I cannot see or read, I must rely on them to tell me what to do, or I must describe what I feel to them.
But right now, my view of the wires is `[?]`. This suggests I haven't "felt" them in detail yet, or the system hasn't populated it.
Actually, looking at standard game mechanics for this type of puzzle: often the Blind monkey starts knowing nothing about the specific properties (like color) because they can't see, but knows physical attributes (like texture, number of strands, etc.). Here, even the wire slots are `[?]`.

Maybe I should try to get information from Mute first?
Mute goes first in the speaking order (Mute, Blind, Deaf).
So Mute has already spoken. But the "VIEWABLE CONTEXT" is empty. This means Mute sent no message, or I missed it?
"You may send several messages in one turn... Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it."
"Mute receives speech from Blind."
"Deaf receives gestures from Blind."

If Mute went first and said nothing useful, or if I just received no input, I need to initiate.
I can speak to Mute. I can gesture to Deaf.

What do I know?
I know there are 3 wires.
I know there is a display and lights.
I don't know the colors (Deaf needs to tell me).
I don't know the rules (Mute needs to tell me).

Strategy:
1. Ask Mute for the rule regarding wires/colors.
2. Ask Deaf for the colors of the wires.

Since I can speak to Mute and gesture to Deaf simultaneously:
To Mute: Speak asking for the cut rule.
To Deaf: Gesture asking for wire colors.

How to ask for colors via gesture?
I can point to the wire positions.
Wire 1, Wire 2, Wire 3.
I can use `👆` (up) or `☝` (one finger) to indicate indices?
Or maybe just point to the general area?
Better: Use numbers. `☝` (1), `✌` (2), `🤟` (3 - wait, 🤟 is ILoveYou sign, usually thumb+index+pinky. In some contexts 3 is middle+ring+pinky or index+middle+ring. Let's stick to simple counting).
Standard gesture alphabet provided:
`☝` (1 finger up)
`✌` (2 fingers)
`🤟` (thumb, index, pinky extended - often used for 3 or ILU)
`🖐` (5 fingers)
`✋` (open hand)
`👆` (point up)
`👇` (point down)
`👈` (point left)
`👉` (point right)

Let's assume `☝`=1, `✌`=2, `🤟`=3 (or maybe `👆` `👆` `👆`?).
Actually, pointing to specific locations might be better if Deaf can see where I'm pointing? No, Deaf sees *me*.
If I gesture `☝` then `🔴` (no red symbol).
I can't name colors.
I need Deaf to tell me the colors.
How does Deaf communicate colors to me?
Deaf can only gesture.
We need a shared code.
Common codes:
Red = ✊ (Fist/Stop/Danger?)
Blue = 👌 (Okay/Calm?)
Yellow = ☝ (Warning?)
Green = 🤟 (Peace/Life?)

This is risky without prior agreement.
However, Mute can read the manual. The manual likely defines the logic.
Logic often depends on color.
Example: "Cut red if light is green".

Step 1: Get the logic from Mute.
Step 2: Get the state from Deaf.

I will speak to Mute asking for the rule.
I will gesture to Deaf asking for the wire configuration. Since we don't have a code, I'll just point to the wires to draw attention, or maybe just wait for Mute's response first?
No, turns are sequential. Mute -> Blind -> Deaf.
Mute spoke. I didn't hear anything (context empty). Maybe Mute waited?
If Mute waited, I should probably ask questions.

Let's try to establish communication.
Speak to Mute: "what is the rule for cutting wires based on colors?"
Gesture to Deaf: Point to wire 1, then wire 2, then wire 3?
Symbols: `👈` (left/wire1?), `👉` (right/wire3?), `☝` (middle/wire2?).
Or just `☝` `✌` `🤟` to represent 1, 2, 3.

Let's send:
Speak to Mute: "rule for wires please"
Gesture to Deaf: ["☝", "✌", "🤟"] (indicating wires 1, 2, 3)

```
speak(to="mute", text="rule for wires please")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Display shows 0. Light is yellow. Wires are 1:yellow, 2:green, 3:blue.

The Deaf monkey has provided the visual state of the bomb:
- Display: 0
- Light: Yellow
- Wires: 1 is Yellow, 2 is Green, 3 is Blue.

I (Blind) can feel the wires but cannot see their colors. I now know which physical wire corresponds to which color based on Deaf's report (assuming standard left-to-right or top-to-bottom ordering, usually Wire 1 is the first one I encounter). However, without knowing the specific rules for this bomb type, I cannot safely cut any wire yet. The manual contains these rules. Mute reads the manual. I need to ask Mute for the rule that applies to a bomb with a yellow light and/or display 0, specifically regarding wire cutting.

I will speak to Mute to request the relevant rule. Since I don't know the specific bomb type name, I'll describe the current state to help Mute find the right section in the manual.

```
speak(to="mute", text="light is yellow display 0 what rule")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Light is now RED. Display is still 0. Wires: 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue.

The state of the bomb has changed: the light is now Red, while the display remains 0. The wire colors are confirmed as Yellow (1), Green (2), and Blue (3). I still lack the specific rule for cutting wires under these conditions (Red Light, Display 0). Mute holds the manual and must provide this information before I can act safely. I will ask Mute for the rule corresponding to a Red light with a Display of 0.

```
speak(to="mute", text="light red display 0 what rule")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Light is now PURPLE. Display is 0. Wires: 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue.

The light color has changed again, now to Purple. The display remains 0 and the wire colors are unchanged (Yellow, Green, Blue). I still do not have the rule for cutting wires under these conditions. Mute must provide the specific instruction for a bomb with a Purple light and Display 0 before I can act safely.

```
speak(to="mute", text="light purple display 0 what rule")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Light is GREEN. Wire 2 is also GREEN. Wires: 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue.

The light is now Green. Wire 2 is also Green. The display was previously reported as 0, but Deaf did not mention it this turn, so I assume it remains 0 or is irrelevant to the current rule trigger. I still lack the specific rule from Mute on how to handle a Green light with these wire colors. Without knowing whether to cut, leave, or which wire to target based on the manual's logic for "Green Light" and "Display 0", any action is a guess that could detonate the bomb. I must wait for Mute to provide the rule.

```
wait()
```

ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Light is ORANGE. Wires are 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. No orange wire.

The light is now Orange. Deaf confirms there is no orange wire (Wires are 1:Yellow, 2:Green, 3:Blue). I still lack the specific rule from Mute for an Orange light. Without knowing if I should cut a specific color, or if the absence of an orange wire triggers a different action, I cannot act safely. I must wait for Mute to provide the manual's instruction for this state.

```
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute signals Wire 2. Cut Wire 2.

Mute has signaled to Deaf that Wire 2 should be cut. Deaf relayed this instruction to me. Since I can feel the wires, I will execute the action on Wire 2 as instructed.

```
act(op="cut", position=2)
```
